title: RestoApp mobile API, the answers of the POS
description: The POS is drawn by the client itself (declaration.schema.json, `client.native`), so its answers are its own shape rather than the list / record envelopes of the universal renderer. This file is that shape, and both sides test against it: the hook validates what `apps/pos.ts` answers, the client keeps a copy in its test resources for `PosOrder`. Order-entry plan: order-entry.plan.md.

posLine.description: A line of the receipt. Every number is core's: nothing is added up on the device.

lineId.description: core's `orderdish.id` — the line, not the product.

oldPrice.description: The price before a promotion took the line; null when none did.

hasOptions.description: The product has modifier groups; core fills their defaults until the chooser exists.

posOrder.description: The draft as the receipt shows it: the state, the way it is received, the lines and the totals the server counted.

placeId.description: The point the order is taken for.

cookingPlaceId.description: Where core decided it is cooked; for a delivery it may be another kitchen.

table.description: Dine-in: the table as the venue calls it (core's `Order.table`, task C12a).

clientId.description: The account the order belongs to; a guest order has none.

date.description: Epoch milliseconds, or null for «as soon as possible».

message.description: What core said about the last recount, verbatim.

posOrderAnswer.description: `pos.order`: one draft when asked by id, otherwise the drafts of this person at this point. `pos.start` answers the same shape with the new draft in `order`.
